paragraphs.text: 1. Kandla–Mundra Port Refining & Maritime Hub (Kutch, Gujarat)
Strategic Role: Globally recognized as the logistics, bulk storage, and maritime export gateway for Indian castor oil. Handles over 70% of total national liquid castor oil and derivative shipments.

Key Facilities: Large automated solvent extraction plants, continuous bleaching refineries, multi-thousand-tonne temperature-controlled liquid shore-tank farms (Adani Wilmar, Jayant Agro, Gokul Agro, Castor Products Company), and dedicated pipeline manifolds connected directly to deepwater liquid cargo jetties at Kandla, Mundra, and Pipavav ports.
Catchment Areas: Receives processed crude oil tankers from expeller plants in Kutch, Surendranagar, Banaskantha, and Rajasthan.

paragraphs.text: 2. North Gujarat Expeller & Assembly Grid (Kadi, Mehsana & Palanpur)
Strategic Role: Center for primary raw seed assembly, commercial spot price discovery, and mechanical first-pressing.

Key Facilities: Dense network of mechanical expeller mills, automated seed cleaning trommels, and de-stoners concentrated across Kadi, Mehsana, Palanpur, Siddhpur, and Deesa; host to the physical delivery points certified by the NCDEX futures exchange.
Catchment Areas: Banaskantha, Patan, Mehsana, Sabarkantha, and cross-border seed arrivals from southern Rajasthan (Jalore, Sirohi, Barmer).

summary.text: In Indian agricultural statistics and global trade economics (Directorate of Economics & Statistics / ICAR-IIOR Hyderabad / SEA of India), Castor Seed (Ricinus communis, locally known as Arandi) is India's most strategically dominant commercial non-edible oilseed crop. India holds an overwhelming global monopoly on castor, accounting for roughly 85% to 90% of total world castor seed and castor oil production, and supplying over 90% of international castor oil export commerce.

passages.text: North Gujarat Belt (Banaskantha, Patan, Mehsana & Sabarkantha) (~52% – 58% of state output):

Kutch is the single largest castor-producing district in India. Sown on arid, light soils under deep tube-well drip systems; the high desert sunshine and dry winters minimize fungal capsule rot, yielding premium-grade bold seeds with high oil content (~49%–51%).
Saurashtra & Central Plains (Surendranagar, Ahmedabad rural & Gandhinagar) (~12% – 16% of state output):
Remaining Districts (~4% – 6%): Junagadh, Rajkot, and Vadodara.
South-Western Arid Belt (Jalore, Barmer & Sirohi) (~74% – 80% of state output):
Remaining Districts (~8% – 12%): Bikaner, Nagaur, and Jaisalmer (along IGNP canal stages).

protection.name: Castor Semilooper (Achaea janata)
protection.geography: National Epidemic Hazard (Heavy in Vegetative Phase across India)
protection.impact: Slender, greyish-brown looper caterpillars with a black stripe and red spots feed voraciously on leaves; early instars skeletonize leaves; older larvae defoliate the plant, leaving only bare stems and midribs (complete defoliation); can destroy an entire field canopy within 5–7 days.
protection.passage: Castor — source table 182, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Castor Shoot & Capsule Borer (Conogethes punctiferalis)
protection.geography: All-India Capsule Setting Phase (Heavy in Nov–January)
protection.impact: Yellow caterpillars with dark spots bore into tender growing shoots, flower buds, and developing green capsules; web together capsules in a spike with silken threads mixed with dark brown frass; feed on ripening seeds within capsules; causes 20–50% yield loss.
protection.passage: Castor — source table 182, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ricini)
protection.geography: All Black-Soil Belts (Soil-Borne) (Severe in Gujarat, Telangana)
protection.impact: Soil-borne systemic vascular wilt; plants show yellowing, drooping, and wilting of leaves from lower branches upward; splitting the main stem longitudinally reveals dark brown-to-black vascular xylem discoloration; affected plants dry up and die; causes 15–70% field mortality.
protection.passage: Castor — source table 182, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Botrytis Grey Mold (Botrytis ricini)
protection.geography: Cloudy, Rainy Intervals (Coastal Gujarat, AP, Telangana)
protection.impact: Infects flowering racemes during humid, cloudy, or rainy weather; spikes are covered by a thick, velvety, bluish-grey fungal mold; flowers rot and drop; green capsules turn soft, black, and rot on the spike ("spike blight"); causes complete loss of flower spikes.
protection.passage: Castor — source table 182, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Sucking Pest Complex: Leafhoppers / Jassids & Thrips (Empoasca flavescens, Retithrips syriacus)
protection.impact:
Jassids: Nymphs and adults suck sap from leaf undersides, injecting toxic saliva; leaf margins curl downward, turn yellow, turn brick-red, and dry up ("Hopper Burn").

Thrips: Lacerate leaf surfaces, causing silvering, crinkling, and premature leaf drop.
protection.passage: Castor — source table 182, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Rust-Red Flour Beetle & Cigarette Beetle (Tribolium castaneum, Lasioderma)
protection.impact: Beetles penetrate broken or cracked seeds; feed on high-lipid endosperm, increasing Free Fatty Acids (FFA) and turning oil rancid; whole unbroken seeds resist storage pests due to their hard, smooth, waxy seed coat.
